$schema_note: Local manufacturing knowledge base: accessory catalog. Configuration data only - installing/removing an accessory here never touches hardware; a human physically attaches or detaches the real accessory and then updates a printer's installed_accessories list in config/manufacturing/printers.json to match.
extensibility_note: Future accessories (filament dryers, cameras, laser modules, cutter modules, additional nozzle/build-plate variants, future printer models' accessories) can be added as new entries here without changing any code - the planner reads whatever capabilities are listed. `factory add-accessory` is planned (see docs/roadmap.md) to do this without hand-editing JSON, but is not implemented in Phase 3.

ams_original.notes: Original-generation AMS. Feeds up to four spools with automatic switching between them during a single print.

ams_2_pro.notes: Newer-generation AMS with improved humidity/moisture control over the original AMS. Installed on the H2D in this fleet.

build_plate_smooth_pei.notes: Default choice for a glossy, smooth part underside; slightly less first-layer grip than textured PEI for large flat parts.

build_plate_textured_pei.notes: Good default for most prints; matte-textured underside, strong first-layer adhesion.

build_plate_engineering.notes: Aimed at higher-temperature engineering materials (e.g. ABS/ASA/PA); improves adhesion for warping-prone filaments.

nozzle_0_2.notes: Best surface detail and small-text legibility; significantly slower and more prone to clogging on abrasive/filled filaments.

nozzle_0_4.notes: Standard default nozzle size; balances detail, strength, and print time for most parts.

nozzle_0_6.notes: Faster for larger, less-detailed parts; loses fine text/detail fidelity versus 0.4mm/0.2mm.

nozzle_0_8.notes: Fastest bulk-material throughput and strongest single-pass layers; coarsest surface detail of the supported sizes.

notes: This file is local reference data only. It never installs, activates, or communicates with any accessory or printer.
A printer's installed_accessories list in config/manufacturing/printers.json is the source of truth for what is actually attached right now; keep it in sync by hand when hardware changes.
